title: Sheffield Hallam University Signs Three MoUs with Indian Institutions in Mumbai and Hyderabad
summary: Sheffield Hallam University has signed MoUs with IISM, Somaiya Vidyavihar University and the ICFAI Foundation for Higher Education to expand research and student exchange with India.
body_html:
New Delhi, 28 October 2026: Sheffield Hallam University has signed three Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with Indian higher education institutions, aiming to strengthen academic collaboration, research and student opportunities between India and the UK. The agreements are with the International Institute of Sports & Management (IISM), Mumbai; Somaiya Vidyavihar University, Mumbai; and the ICFAI Foundation for Higher Education (IFHE), Hyderabad.

The MoUs were signed during the university's participation in the Great North trade mission to India. They provide a framework to explore joint research, student and staff exchanges, progression pathways, programme development and knowledge exchange.

"We are delighted to be strengthening our relationships with India through these new and renewed partnerships. This landmark trade mission has provided an important opportunity to deepen our connections, celebrate our shared ambitions and build new opportunities for collaboration," said Professor Liz Mossop, Vice-Chancellor of Sheffield Hallam University.

Sheffield Hallam has renewed its MoU with the ICFAI Foundation for Higher Education in Hyderabad. Sheffield Business School and its Indian counterpart will explore progression routes, study-abroad opportunities, virtual engagement and summer schools. Dr Sam Giove, Director of Sheffield Business School, said the renewal "reflects our ambition to strengthen ties with prestigious Indian business schools that share our mission and vision."

The university has also renewed its MoU with IISM, Mumbai, building on an established relationship. The partnership brings together IISM's expertise in sports management and sports science with Sheffield Hallam's strengths in sport education, applied research, sports engineering and physical activity, and will explore joint research, student and staff mobility, progression routes, programme development and industry engagement. "Our priority now is to translate the MoU into meaningful opportunities for students, staff and our partners," said Dr Ruth M Crabtree, Head of the School of Sport and Physical Activity at Sheffield Hallam University.

A new institution-wide MoU with Somaiya Vidyavihar University will support discussions on joint research, staff and student exchange, progression arrangements and joint programme development across the university.

The visit comes as India and the UK deepen economic and educational ties following the UK–India Free Trade Agreement, which came into force in July 2026. The trade mission brought nearly 200 representatives from northern England to build partnerships with Indian universities, businesses and institutions, with a four-day programme across New Delhi, Hyderabad and Mumbai. Sheffield Hallam said the next phase will focus on turning the agreements into practical initiatives for students, academics and researchers in both countries.
